caption:
foundit's Appraisal Trends Report 2026: 52% of Indian professionals are actively job-hunting, 96% are open to switching. Most of them did the work. The rating didn't reflect it.

Here is the hard part. A new employer inherits the same you. Same bearing in the room. Same rushed answer when the senior-most person turns to you. Same habit of filling silence before your point lands. The pattern travels. It gets on the plane with you.

Appraisals rarely measure competence alone. They measure what the room remembers of you. If your idea only registers when someone else repeats it louder, that is not a company problem. That is a carriage problem, and it follows you to the next desk.

In command, you learn that authority is transmitted before you speak — through posture, pace, and the discipline to hold a pause. Those are trainable. Fix the pattern first. Then interview.

topic.title: The appraisal hangover: switching jobs won't fix the pattern
topic.angle: These are competent people whose appraisal outcome didn't match their contribution — exactly Lumina's thesis that recognition fails on how competence is carried, and that the pattern travels with you to the next employer.
topic.why_now: foundit's Appraisal Trends Report 2026 found 52% actively job-hunting and 96% open to switching, and that mid-year cohort is interviewing right now inside the Q4 hiring window.

rationale: A stark, text-only visual matches the no-nonsense command tone and keeps the single hard idea — the pattern follows you — front and centre.
